rationale: A 142-person concentrated spearmint extract trial reported inconclusive sleep comparisons, while a smaller separate trial favored sleep initiation. Preliminary and final reports of one spearmint and green-tea blend trial show some favorable insomnia scores with inconclusive primary sleep outcomes. These exposures and populations leave a dried spearmint effect on Parkinson insomnia unresolved.

Anxiety values and the exact statistical contrast are unavailable for the refined sunflower and sesame comparison. A separate depression trial combines oral sunflower oil with positive suggestion and reports composite well-being including relaxation, without an isolated anxiety outcome. Neither study identifies a cold-pressed sunflower effect on Parkinson anxiety.

The longer controlled tart cherry concentrate study favors mental fatigue during a cognitive task, while a separate acute 27-person crossover gives inconclusive fatigue ratings. Other comparisons are inconclusive and include an insomnia trial with a numerically unfavorable difference. The evidence gives a minimal lean against worsening, with transfer from concentrate and task fatigue to dried fruit and Parkinson fatigue uncertain.

Some corn-oil recipients improved on the Hamilton scale in the Parkinson trial, with the group comparison favoring DHA plus EPA. In other populations, separate corn versus fish-oil studies give mixed or inconclusive depression contrasts, often with both groups taking antidepressants. The retrieved Parkinson preview still leaves the outcome table and corn grade unresolved. The studies lack an oil-free comparator.

A dried mango crossover measured glucose and appetite without depressive severity. The newer experiment offers dried mango among optional snacks and reports only aggregate intake and momentary affect. Fresh-mango and MiniMeal protocols have no posted depression results. The mango leaf extract trials give mixed mood estimates. An isolated dried mango effect on Parkinson depressive symptoms remains unresolved.
